blocks.text: Imagine a social network where each person is a node and each friendship is an edge. How do we efficiently represent this network for analysis?

blocks.markdown: Graphs are fundamental structures used to model pairwise relations between objects. In computer science, graphs are used to represent networks of communication, data organization, computational devices, and more. Two common ways to represent graphs are adjacency matrices and adjacency lists.

blocks.title: Graph
blocks.text: A graph $G = (V, E)$ consists of a set of vertices $V$ and a set of edges $E$ where each edge connects two vertices.

blocks.markdown:
### Adjacency Matrix
An adjacency matrix is a 2D array of size $|V| \times |V|$ where $|V|$ is the number of vertices in the graph. The element at row $i$ and column $j$ is $1$ if there is an edge from vertex $i$ to vertex $j$, and $0$ otherwise.

blocks.latex: A[i][j] = \begin{cases} 1, & \text{if there is an edge from } i \text{ to } j \\ 0, & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
blocks.caption: Adjacency Matrix Definition

blocks.title: Building an Adjacency Matrix
blocks.prompt: Construct the adjacency matrix for a graph with vertices $A, B, C$ and edges $(A, B), (B, C), (C, A)$. Assume the vertices are labeled as $0, 1, 2$ respectively.

steps.text: Set $A[0][1] = 1$ for edge $(A, B)$, $A[1][2] = 1$ for edge $(B, C)$, and $A[2][0] = 1$ for edge $(C, A)$.

blocks.markdown:
### Adjacency List
An adjacency list represents a graph as an array of lists. The index of the array represents a vertex, and each element in the list represents the vertices adjacent to the vertex.

blocks.title: Building an Adjacency List
blocks.prompt: Construct the adjacency list for the same graph with vertices $A, B, C$ and edges $(A, B), (B, C), (C, A)$. Assume the vertices are labeled as $0, 1, 2$ respectively.

steps.text: Initialize an array with three empty lists: $[[], [], []]$.
Add $1$ to the list at index $0$ for edge $(A, B)$, $2$ to the list at index $1$ for edge $(B, C)$, and $0$ to the list at index $2$ for edge $(C, A)$.

blocks.markdown:
### Space and Time Trade-offs
The choice between adjacency matrix and adjacency list depends on the graph's density. A dense graph has many edges, while a sparse graph has relatively few. The adjacency matrix is suitable for dense graphs due to its $O(|V|^2)$ space complexity, whereas the adjacency list is more efficient for sparse graphs with $O(|V| + |E|)$ space complexity.

blocks.title: Enumerating Neighbours
blocks.text: Enumerating all neighbours of a vertex is $O(|V|)$ in an adjacency matrix and $O(d)$ in an adjacency list, where $d$ is the degree of the vertex.

points: Adjacency matrices and lists are two primary graph representations.
Adjacency matrices are space-efficient for dense graphs, while adjacency lists are better for sparse graphs.
Enumerating a vertex's neighbours is faster in an adjacency list for sparse graphs.
